_source: J. J. Potoff and A. Z. Panagiotopoulos, J. Chem. Phys. 109, 10914 (1998), doi:10.1063/1.477787 (primary); J. Perez-Pellitero, P. Ungerer, G. Orkoulas, A. D. Mackie, J. Chem. Phys. 125, 054515 (2006), doi:10.1063/1.2227027 (independent confirmation, Table II)
_system: binary Lennard-Jones, sigma_1 = sigma_2 = 1.0, eps_1 = 1.0, eps_2 = 0.5, Lorentz-Berthelot cross terms
_units: T* = kT/eps_11, rho* = N sigma_11^3/V, p* = p sigma_11^3/eps_11, x1 = mole fraction of component 1 (the eps=1, i.e. STRONGER, species) — same convention as critical_line_s2lj.py
_extracted: 2026-07-28, from pdf/sources_paywall/. P&P values are the paper's own summary in Sec. V (p. 10920); the 2006 values are its Table II.

mixture_critical_point_at_T1._method: mixed-field finite-size scaling, extrapolated to L=inf (V = 216 ... 1728)
mixture_critical_point_at_T1._spread: Across the four estimates: x1_c 0.458-0.49, rho*_c 0.39-0.406, p*_c 0.151-0.1522. The first three agree closely; the cumulant-intersection row is the outlier the 2006 authors themselves flag as least accurate for the mixture.

coexistence_table_I._source: P&P 1998 Table I, p. 10920 — 'Selected phase coexistence data'. Parentheses = uncertainty in the last digit.
coexistence_table_I._note: Vapour-liquid coexistence, not spinodal. Comparing against it needs a phase-equilibrium solve (equal mu_i and p between phases), which the current spinodal/critical machinery does not do.

mixture_critical_line._note: Neither paper tabulates T_c versus composition. P&P give the single critical point at T*=1.0; the 2006 paper's Fig. 6 shows p-x-y diagrams at T*=0.86, 1.00 and 1.14 with the critical point marked on each, so three points of the critical line could be digitised from that figure if needed.
